takeaway: Pringle's manoeuvre grasps the free edge of the lesser omentum, compressing the hepatic artery and portal vein (b and c only) to control liver bleeding.

lines.text: A young man with a liver laceration is bleeding heavily.
Pringle's manoeuvre means grasping the free edge of the lesser omentum.
Within that free edge lies the hepatic artery,
Compressing them stops blood reaching the liver, so the haemorrhage can be controlled.
lines.say: Compressing them stops blood reaching the liver, so the haemorrhage can be controlled. (sigh)

lines.text: The superior mesenteric artery is not compressed.
So the answer is b and c only: the hepatic artery and the portal vein.
lines.say: So the answer is b and c only: the hepatic artery, and the portal vein.
